record.original_question: In recovery problems with noisy data, why do semidefinite-programming relaxations of maximum-likelihood estimators often remain tight beyond the exact-recovery regime? More concretely, when noise is large enough that the maximum-likelihood estimator cannot exactly recover the ground truth, under what structural or probabilistic conditions does the SDP relaxation still return a solution that lies in the original nonconvex model class, or equivalently matches the lower-rank quasi-maximum-likelihood solution instead of requiring a rounding step?

evidence.quote: We have observed an interesting, yet unexplained, phenomenon: Semidefinite programming (SDP) based relaxations of maximum likelihood estimators (MLE) tend to be tight in recovery problems with noisy data, even when MLE cannot exactly recover the ground truth.
However, to the best of our knowledge, their tightness is not understood beyond this regime.
Yet, to the best of our knowledge, there is no theoretical understanding of this rank recovery phenomenon.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let an unknown ground-truth signal x* belong to a nonconvex set M (for example, a product of unit spheres, a group such as O(d), U(d), or SO(d), or the discrete cube {±1}^n). Suppose noisy measurements C are obtained (e.g., C = x*x*^T + σW for a symmetric noise matrix W) and consider the maximum-likelihood estimator

  x_MLE ∈ argmin_{x ∈ M} f(x; C),

where f is the negative log-likelihood, typically a quadratic form in a rank-one or low-rank lift X = xx^T. The standard semidefinite relaxation is

  X_SDP ∈ argmin_{X ⪰ 0, X ∈ K} ⟨L(C), X⟩,

where K encodes the linear constraints (e.g., diag(X) = I) and L(C) is the data matrix associated with f.

The relaxation is called tight when X_SDP has the same rank as the lift x*x*^T of any feasible point of M (so X_SDP corresponds to an actual element of M, with no rounding step required); equivalently, X_SDP coincides with the lift of the quasi-MLE on M.

It is known that in the low-noise (exact-recovery) regime, where x_MLE = x*, the SDP relaxation is tight. Empirically, however, SDP tightness persists well beyond this regime: even when the noise is large enough that x_MLE ≠ x*, the optimum X_SDP still has the appropriate low rank and equals the lift of x_MLE.

Problem. Identify general structural and/or probabilistic conditions on M, on the cost function f, and on the noise model under which the following rank-recovery phenomenon holds with high probability: the optimal solution X_SDP of the SDP relaxation lies in the lifted nonconvex feasible set {xx^T : x ∈ M} (equivalently, has the rank of a lifted point of M), and hence equals the lift of the (quasi-)MLE on M, throughout a noise regime strictly larger than the exact-recovery regime. Provide a theoretical explanation of this tightness beyond the exact-recovery threshold.
artifact.status_search_result: The general phenomenon was posed as an open problem and remains without a unified explanation. Partial progress exists: Bandeira, Boumal, and Singer (arXiv:1411.3272) established a rank-recovery / tightness result for the angular synchronization SDP beyond exact recovery, and subsequent work (e.g., on Z2 synchronization and graph clustering, including a 2025 paper in Information and Inference) has analyzed benign nonconvex landscapes near exact-recovery thresholds. A general theory covering the broad class of recovery SDPs is still lacking.

status_evidence.title: Tightness of the maximum likelihood semidefinite relaxation for angular synchronization
status_evidence.snippet: First instance establishing a rank-recovery/tightness result for an SDP relaxation beyond the exact-recovery regime, for angular synchronization.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: tightness/rank-recovery established for angular synchronization.

status_evidence.title: Nonconvex landscapes for Z2 synchronization and graph clustering are benign near exact recovery thresholds
status_evidence.snippet: Analyzes benign nonconvex landscapes near exact-recovery thresholds for Z2 synchronization and graph clustering.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial progress on related models near exact-recovery thresholds.

status_evidence.title: Open problem: Tightness of maximum likelihood semidefinite relaxations
status_evidence.snippet: Posed as an open problem with the phenomenon unexplained beyond the exact-recovery regime.
status_evidence.claim: Original problem statement; phenomenon left open in general.
